data.title: Substrate-selective mTORC1 regulation and gene dosage-dependent tissue divergence in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome
data.authors: Cao ZL; Zhao SC; Lin F; Liu YH; Hong XT; Hong LY; Xu LQ; Li FP; Yu HY; Yao WG; Chen WY

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Narrative synthesis (human genetics + mouse mechanistic data)
data.finding: Reframes Birt-Hogg-Dube (BHD) syndrome beyond the classic 'global mTORC1 hyperactivation' model: FLCN acts as a GAP for RagC/D, giving substrate-selective (not global) mTORC1 control. Biallelic FLCN loss drives kidney tumors via MiT/TFE nuclear accumulation, while haploinsufficiency alone is sufficient for lung and skin lesions -- resolving the 'mTORC1 paradox' via gene dosage and signaling timing. Narrative synthesis of human genetics and mouse mechanistic data.
data.abstract_excerpt: Birt-Hogg-Dube (BHD) syndrome, caused by mutations in the tumor suppressor gene, has traditionally been classified as a classic 'mTORopathy' characterized by global mTORC1 activation. Recent structural and multi-omic studies have fundamentally challenged this view, revealing that FLCN functions as a GAP for RagC/D to govern substrate-selective mTORC1 regulation.

extracted_findings.effect: Argues that FLCN loss produces substrate-selective rather than global mTORC1 activation, with biallelic loss driving renal tumours via nuclear MiT/TFE and haploinsufficiency sufficing for lung and skin lesions.
